svg.aria-label: The deployment path in order: thirteen numbered steps grouped into prepare, server, software, secrets, run and go-live, each with the command to run and the check that proves it is done, with a mandatory secret-rotation gate before going live.

g.text: PREPARE · AWS ACCOUNT
Create the AWS account and a safe admin login
Turn on MFA for the root user, delete any root access keys — then stop using root for daily work.
Create an IAM user (e.g. smaart-admin) with AdministratorAccess + MFA and sign in with that from now on.
DONE WHEN
You are signed in as the IAM user, not root.
Root shows MFA enabled and zero access keys.
SERVER
Launch the EC2 server and give it a fixed address
EC2 → Launch instance: Ubuntu 22.04 LTS · t3.small (2 GB RAM) · 20–30 GB disk. Create and download the key pair
smaart.pem.
Allocate an Elastic IP and associate it with the instance — this is the <EIP> used in every step below.
DONE WHEN
Instance shows 2/2 status checks.
Elastic IP is attached and never changes on reboot.
Set the Security Group — the firewall
Inbound rules, exactly three: SSH 22 from YOUR IP only · HTTP 80 from anywhere · HTTPS 443 from anywhere.
Never open 5000 or 5001 — only Nginx on the same machine talks to those.
DONE WHEN
The Inbound tab lists three rules and nothing else.
Connect from Windows PowerShell
icacls smaart.pem /inheritance:r /grant:r "%USERNAME%:R"
ssh -i smaart.pem ubuntu@<EIP>
sudo apt update && sudo apt upgrade -y
DONE WHEN
The prompt reads ubuntu@ip-… and apt finishes without errors.
SOFTWARE
Install Node.js, git, Nginx and pm2
Node.js LTS via the NodeSource setup script, the rest with apt, pm2 globally with npm.
sudo apt install -y git nginx && sudo npm install -g pm2
DONE WHEN
node -v · git --version · nginx -v · pm2 -v all print a version.
Clone both repos into /var/www and install dependencies
Add a read-only deploy SSH key on GitHub for each repo. Clone SMAART-INSTITUE-USERDASHBOARD and ADMIN-SMAART-INSTITUTE-26.
Run npm install in all four folders: back-end/ and front-end/ (user) · Backend/ and Frontend/ (admin).
cd /var/www && git clone git@github.com:<org>/<repo>.git
DONE WHEN
Both repos exist under /var/www and each of the four folders has node_modules.
SECRETS
Create the two .env files by hand on the server — never in git
User back-end/.env → PORT=5000 · Admin Backend/.env → PORT=5001 · both NODE_ENV=production.
MONGODB_URI, JWT_SECRET (64+ hex chars) and ADMIN_SYSTEM_SECRET must be IDENTICAL in both files. Add Cloudinary, SMTP and
OpenRouter keys.
The variable is MONGODB_URI — the guide’s sample .env says MONGO_URI, which the code does not read.
chmod 600 back-end/.env (and Backend/.env in the admin repo)
DONE WHEN
.env is listed in both .gitignore files.
ls -l shows -rw------- on each .env.
MongoDB Atlas → Network Access lists only <EIP>.
Gate — rotate every secret before go-live. They were once committed to git, so treat every current value as leaked.
1 MongoDB Atlas → Database Access → Edit Password → put the new MONGODB_URI in BOTH .env files
2 openssl rand -hex 48 → new JWT_SECRET, same in both (logs everyone out — that is the point)
3 openssl rand -hex 48 → new ADMIN_SYSTEM_SECRET, same in both
4 New Cloudinary key pair · new OpenRouter key · new Deepgram key · new SMTP app password
5 Delete or disable every OLD key at its source — rotation is not finished until the old value is dead
RUN
Start both back-ends under pm2
cd /var/www/SMAART-INSTITUE-USERDASHBOARD/back-end && pm2 start server.js --name user-backend
cd /var/www/ADMIN-SMAART-INSTITUTE-26/Backend && pm2 start server.js --name admin-backend
pm2 startup → run the sudo command it prints → pm2 save
DONE WHEN
pm2 status shows both online with 0 restarts.
pm2 logs shows “MongoDB connected” for each.
Build both front-ends
Set VITE_API_URL / REACT_APP_API_URL to the production domain BEFORE building — they are baked into the bundle.
On small RAM add a 2 GB swapfile first, or the CRA build gets killed out-of-memory.
cd front-end && npm run build → dist/
cd Frontend && npm run build → build/
DONE WHEN
front-end/dist and Frontend/build exist and each contains index.html.
Configure Nginx — one server block per site
smaart-user: server_name yourdomain.com www.yourdomain.com · root …/front-end/dist · /api/ and /socket.io/ →
smaart-admin: server_name admin.yourdomain.com · root …/Frontend/build · /api/ → 127.0.0.1:5001
try_files $uri /index.html keeps React Router working. Symlink both into sites-enabled, remove default.
sudo nginx -t && sudo systemctl reload nginx
DONE WHEN
nginx -t prints “syntax is ok · test is successful”.
http://<EIP> shows the User Dashboard.
GO LIVE
Point the Hostinger domain at the server
hPanel → Domains → DNS records: A @ → <EIP> · A www → <EIP> · A admin → <EIP>. Delete old parking A / CNAME records.
nslookup yourdomain.com nslookup admin.yourdomain.com
DONE WHEN
Both lookups return <EIP> — can take minutes to a few hours.
Free HTTPS for all three names
sudo snap install --classic certbot
sudo certbot --nginx -d yourdomain.com -d www.yourdomain.com -d admin.yourdomain.com
sudo certbot renew --dry-run
DONE WHEN
Both sites load with the padlock.
http:// redirects to https:// automatically.
The dry-run ends with “success”.
Final production checks
Confirm NODE_ENV=production in both .env files, reload the environment into pm2, then prove it survives a reboot.
pm2 restart all --update-env && pm2 save
sudo reboot → wait 2 min → ssh back in → pm2 status
DONE WHEN
Student login works (proves /api + Atlas).
Real-time features work (proves /socket.io).
Admin login works (proves port 5001).
After the reboot both apps are online with no manual action.
LIVE · https://yourdomain.com = User Dashboard · https://admin.yourdomain.com = Admin Dashboard
Shipping an update afterwards
ssh in → cd into the repo → git pull → npm install if dependencies changed →
npm run build for a front-end change · pm2 restart user-backend / admin-backend for a back-end change.
Never edit code on the server. Or let GitHub Actions do it — deploy-ec2.yml and deploy-admin-ec2.yml already exist.
Safe to skip for now
Docker · ECR · ECS/Fargate · Load balancer · Auto Scaling · Route 53 · Secrets Manager.
All of it is for the day one server is not enough. Keep DNS on Hostinger.
One exception worth doing now: a CloudWatch billing alarm so the bill cannot surprise you.
